A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MLE-STAR and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-J. The complete documents support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original MLE-STAR evaluations on MLE-bench Lite and tabular competitions, along with ensemble and checker ablations, refinement trajectories, and an appendix contamination analysis.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds benchmark-wide Gemini-2.5-Pro results and four-task Claude-Sonnet-4 results.

M1.justification: The retrieval, targeted refinement, ensembling, debugging, and data-checking procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A-B. The additional LLM configurations are experimental variants; no procedural adaptation is documented.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 22 MLE-bench Lite competitions and four additional tabular competitions listed in Appendix E. The revised reasoning-model experiment retains DDD, DBI, SAI, and WCR; testing additional LLMs introduces no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged: AIDE, MLAB, and OpenHands in Table 1, DS-Agent in Table 2, and AutoGluon and DS-Agent configurations in Appendix G. Ensemble comparators in Table 4 also remain unchanged. Claude-Sonnet-4 is another MLE-STAR configuration, not an added competing method.

E3.justification: Gemini-2.5-Pro evaluation expands from four competitions to the full 22-competition benchmark, and Claude-Sonnet-4 replaces it in Table 3's four-task experiment. These extend the tested model configurations while retaining the metrics, 24-hour limit, and refinement and ensemble budgets.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 broadens the analysis of dependence on the underlying LLM through benchmark-wide Gemini-2.5-Pro results and a Claude-Sonnet-4 experiment. Ensemble ablations, checker analyses, refinement trajectories, and the appendix contamination analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The three-seed convention, five-seed DS-Agent comparison, and Table 1 exceptions of 16 and 36 seeds remain unchanged. Table 1 continues reporting means with one standard error, while Table 3 continues reporting point estimates; no statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds benchmark-wide Gemini-2.5-Pro results, including 63.6±6.0% any medal and 36.4±6.0% gold; the Flash results remain 43.9±6.2% and 30.3±5.7%. Table 3 removes four Pro scores and reports Sonnet-4 scores instead: for example, DDD RMSE is 0.0196 for Pro in v1 and 0.0155 for Sonnet-4 in v2, while WCR AUROC is respectively 0.9939 and 0.9888. These substantially extend and replace results under different model configurations, rather than improve the retained configuration.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, equations (1)-(11), and Algorithms 1-3 remain unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract's headline medal rate changes from 44% to 64%, and the conclusion's gold rate changes from 30% to 36%. Both now explicitly identify MLE-bench Lite. The introduction updates its comparison from 25.8% versus 43.9% to 25.8% versus 63.6%, while the methodological contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds an interpretation that the Claude-Sonnet-4 results demonstrate compatibility and generalizability beyond Gemini models. V1's interpretation concerned benefiting from stronger reasoning models. Existing mechanism explanations, failure discussions, and the contamination limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The appendices retain the same prompts, implementation instructions, subsampling rules, hardware, runtime information, and repository references. V2's explicit Gemini-2.0-Flash default and DS-Agent-comparison wording restate configurations already identified in v1's tables and appendices.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix J, and the reference list remain unchanged. The positioning against AutoML, code-space exploration, and manually curated case banks is retained without added citations or revised novelty claims.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the headline statements, setup clarifications, and the rewritten reasoning-model paragraph in Section 4.2; the overall structure remains intact. The new paragraph introduces repetition, typographical errors, and the inappropriate phrase 'to further address your comments.'

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a model row and changes its emphasis, while Table 3 receives a new caption and model headers. Table spacing, page breaks, and footer placement change slightly. The figures and appendix displays retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: Evaluating Gemini-2.5-Pro across all 22 competitions and adding Claude-Sonnet-4 results provides broader empirical support for operation across underlying LLMs, while retaining the original matched Flash comparison. Explicitly naming MLE-bench Lite also clarifies scope. These gains outweigh limited reporting losses: four Pro task scores disappear, the new prose is poorly edited, and the introduction's updated 25.8%-versus-63.6% comparison mixes underlying models and therefore does not isolate the agent's contribution.
